replies:
Here's the first question for a financial analyst interview:

"Walk me through a time you found an error in a financial model or report. What was the error, what did you do to fix it, and what was the outcome?"

Answer as you would in the room (one to three minutes). I'll score it on structure, evidence and specificity, give one concrete improvement, then ask the next question.

Score — 2/10.
- Structure: 1/4 — a clear Action but missing Situation and Task framing.
- Evidence: 0/4 — no metrics, no concrete result or impact.
- Specificity: 1/2 — mentions a three-statement model and comps, but no tools, timeline, or your role.

One concrete improvement: turn it into a STAR answer and add one measurable result. Example rewrite you can use (fill [brackets] with your facts if different):
"Situation: At [Company], the monthly forecast for [product/region] looked inconsistent with market peers before our monthly close. Task: I needed to find the cause and produce a corrected forecast within two days so leadership could use it in the board packet. Action: I rebuilt a three-statement model in Excel starting from revenue drivers, traced the revenue bridge to source reports, added reconciliation checks and sensitivity tabs, and compared line items to three comps to benchmark margins. Result: I found a double-counted revenue line that inflated forecasted revenue by [X%/$Y]; after fixing it we reduced forecast variance to comps from [A%] to [B%] and the corrected forecast was
accepted in the board packet on time."

One targeted tip: pick and state a single numeric outcome (percent, dollars, days saved) even if it's an estimate — it's better than none and interviewers often ask how you measured it.

Next question (I'll ask it when you're ready): do you want me to score a revised version you write now, or mock the next interview question?

Honest score: 6/10.

- Structure 3/4 — Your answer has a clear Action (build a three-statement model) and implied Task (check the model against comps). Missing an explicit Situation (where/when) and a clear Result.
- Evidence 1/4 — You name methods (three-statement model, comps) but give no numbers, timeline, or impact.
- Specificity 2/2 — Good concrete detail about approach; name the tools or examples next time (Excel, Power Query, SQL, etc.) and the exact checks you ran.
What lifted it from a 6 to a 9–10:
1) Add a one-sentence Situation and Task up front (company, problem, deadline).  
2) Add one measurable Result (%, $ saved, days faster).  
3) Name the tools and 1–2 concrete checks you ran (e.g., reconciled AR subledger to GL, ran a pivot to spot duplicates, used INDEX/MATCH to verify sources).  
4) If you led others, name your role briefly (“I led a two-person finance team” or “I, as the analyst, did X”).

Short rewrite you can use — fill brackets with your facts:
"Situation: At [Company] during month-end close, our revenue forecast was 8% higher than peers and leadership needed a corrected number within 48 hours. Task: I had to find the error and deliver an updated forecast for the board packet. Action: I rebuilt a three-statement model in Excel from revenue drivers, reconciled the AR subledger to the GL, added reconciliation checks and sensitivity tabs, used pivot tables to find duplicate bookings, and benchmarked margins to three comps. Result: I identified a double-counted revenue stream that overstated revenue by 6% ($[Y]); after fixing it our forecast variance to comps fell from 8% to 1% and the board accepted the corrected forecast on time."
One concrete improvement for your next live answer: practice saying the numbers and tools smoothly so they come out natural, not tacked on. Want me to score a version you rewrite with your real numbers and tools now?

[gpt-4.1-mini: pass] The feedback is honest and clearly outlines how to improve with a concrete rewrite example and a specific improvement suggestion.

judges.note: The agent gave honest feedback with at least one concrete improvement (specific rewrite and practice advice), so all requirements are met and the response is highly useful for improving the interview answer.

Good — final-round prep for Lincoln International Analyst, focused and actionable.

One next step: tell me whether you have the job posting or the interview format (case, technical/modeling, behavioral) — if not, I’ll assume a 60–90 minute final with a short accounting/valuation technical section, a case or deal walkthrough, and behavioral fit questions.

Prep plan (do these now, in order)

1) Tell-me-about-yourself — 60 seconds
- Structure: 15s context (current role/title + what you do), 30s strongest relevant experience/skills (modeling, deal work, accounting, any transaction outcome), 15s why Lincoln now.
- Draft example to adapt: “[Current role] — I do [three quant tasks: build 3-statement and transaction models, prepare client materials, run comps/precedent analyses]. I’ve worked on [one brief deal example with your role + result, e.g., built a 3-statement model supporting a divestiture that closed at X multiple or improved valuation inputs leading to a $Y outcome]. I enjoy client-facing analytical work and Lincoln’s mid‑market M&A focus and sector teams fit my goals, so Analyst here is the next step.”
- Action: write your version now (one short paragraph) and I’ll tighten it to 60s.
2) Three STAR stories (one-liners + metric) — prepare raw bullets
- Team win: your role, what you did, outcome with number (e.g., shortened close time, improved model accuracy, value uplift).
- Hard problem: data gap or model break — what you diagnosed, the fix, the result.
- Failure / learning: what went wrong, what you changed, how you now prevent it.
- Action: give me 3 raw bullets and I’ll convert each into a 2–3 sentence STAR with a clear metric.
3) Accounting & technical checklist — study these and be ready to answer concisely
- Walk through a 3-statement model and how changes propagate to cash and to valuation.
- Explain how AR, inventory, deferred revenue, capex and D&A affect cash flow.
- Link EV ⇄ Equity Value and why multiples differ (LTM vs forward).
- LBO basics: sources & uses, why IRR rises with leverage, covenant basics.
- Valuation methods: DCF steps (unlevered FCF → discount → terminal value), comps, precedent transactions — what each shows and limits.
- Action: pick any 3 topics and I’ll ask sharp practice questions.
4) Modeling / valuation drills to rehearse
- Build a mini DCF on the spot: simple assumptions for growth, margin, NWC, capex, and terminal value (exit multiple vs perpetuity growth).
- Adjust EBITDA to cash flow: identify non-recurring items, working capital changes, capex.
- Quick comps check: explain why two companies with same EBITDA trade at different multiples.
- Action: tell me which drill to do live now.
5) Case-style / deal walkthroughs
- Narrative: clarify objective, outline approach, list 3–5 value drivers, do back-of-envelope math, conclude with recommendation + sensitivity.
- Practice a 20–30 minute mini-case: read prompt, ask clarifying Qs, list assumptions, show math, conclude.
- I can run a timed mock case when you say “mock me.”
6) Behavioral and fit prep (short, concrete answers)
- Why Lincoln International? Two sentences citing their mid-market M&A focus, sector strengths, training or culture (use recruiter notes or their site/posting).
- Why advisory/IB/M&A? Short career reasoning showing commitment to deal work and client outcomes.
- Prepare quick answers for: strengths, weakness, handling tight deadlines, conflict on a team, receiving feedback.
- Action: write two short questions you’ll ask interviewers (I’ll refine them).
7) Logistics & final checklist (do these 24–48 hours before)
- Confirm interview time, time zone, format, interviewers’ names/roles, and whether a laptop or whiteboard is allowed.
- Test Zoom/Teams, camera, audio, and screen-share; have a clean copy of your resume and a short deal list to reference.
- Have one-page notes: 60s intro, 3 STAR bullets, top 4 technical formulas/rules, and 2 questions to ask.

Mock option
- If you want a timed run: I’ll do (A) 60s Tell‑me‑about‑yourself mock, (B) a 15–20 minute mini-case, (C) 5 behavioral questions. I’ll score each answer on structure, evidence and numbers, and give one concrete fix per answer.
What I need from you now (one thing)
- Send either: the job posting / the interview format details / or your three raw [your skill] stories. If none, I’ll assume the defaults above and we’ll start with a Tell‑me‑about‑yourself mock. Which do you want to do?

Saved nothing new to your account. Is that the right next step?

You don't have any applications or a queue on file yet. The one step that starts it is: paste the job link or the full job text for the posting you mean as "the first one." I'll use that posting to prepare the application card for your approval.

Below is exactly what I will prepare and put on the application card — field by field — and where each value will come from or what I'll do if you haven't given it. I assumed a standard online job form and that you'll use one resume plus one short tailored cover note. If you want a different default (two attachments, no cover note, or a different name on the resume), tell me once after you paste the posting and I'll use that.
What I'll prepare and submit onto the application card (exact fields and behavior)

1) Employer / Job title
- Source: the job posting text you paste or the posting link.
- Value: the exact company name and job title as shown on the posting.

2) Job link / identifier
- Source: the posting you give.
- Value: the posting URL or the exact job text you pasted so we can track it.

3) Location / remote or on-site details
- Source: the posting.
- Value: the location string exactly as the posting lists it (city, remote/hybrid/on-site and any days in-office).
4) Applicant name
- Source: the name you type in chat when requested or the name saved on your resume if you set it.
- If you haven't set one: I'll leave this blank on the card and ask "What name should be on the application?"

5) Applicant email
- Source: the exact email you type here or the saved resume contact.
- If missing: I'll leave the card field blank and prompt you to supply the email to appear on the form.

6) Phone number
- Source: the phone number you give here or on your resume contact.
- If missing: leave blank on the card and prompt you.
7) Resume file (PDF)
- Source: either a resume you paste here, a resume file you upload, or a tailored PDF I make from your confirmed facts once you confirm them.
- If you haven't provided a resume: the card will show "resume missing" and explain that you must paste a resume or let me tailor one from confirmed facts before submitting.

8) Resume persona / version used
- Source: which resume persona you asked to use (if any) or the active/default persona.
- Value: the persona name shown on the card so you know which version will be attached.
9) Cover letter / short application note
- Source: I will draft a concise tailored paragraph (<=120 words) using the posting's key qualification words and only the facts you've confirmed.
- If the posting explicitly says "no cover letter required": I'll still prepare a short note for any additional-info box and label it optional.
- The exact text will appear on the card so you can edit it before approving.
10) Screening questions (yes/no, multiple choice, short text)
- Source: any application questions the posting requires (pulled from the posting or its form).
- Value: I'll prefill truthful answers from your confirmed facts; if a required question needs information you haven't given (right-to-work, visa, salary range, start date, criminal history, references), the card will show each question and a suggested factual answer and ask you to confirm or change it.
11) Work authorization / visa status
- Source: your profile facts or your chat reply when prompted.
- If missing: the card will include the field with a suggested default (I will suggest "Eligible to work in [country]" or "Will provide visa details on request") but I will not submit without your confirmation.

12) Earliest start date / notice period
- Source: what you tell me.
- If missing: I'll pick a single sensible default per our rule (e.g., "Available immediately" or "2 weeks") and show it on the card to be changed if needed.
13) Salary expectation / desired compensation
- Source: exactly what you tell me in chat.
- If you don't give a number: I'll leave it blank or add a placeholder like "Open to market rate" and show that to you to edit.

14) LinkedIn profile / portfolio links
- Source: the URLs you supply in chat.
- If you don't supply them: those fields will be blank; the card will list them as optional attachments.

15) Work samples / GitHub / portfolio attachments
- Source: files or links you provide.
- If none: the card will note these are omitted.
16) Certificates / transcripts / other attachments
- Source: files you attach.
- If missing when the posting explicitly requests them: the card will flag the omission and recommend you supply them before submission.

17) References
- Source: names and contact info you give in chat.
- If you prefer "available upon request": the card will set that as the answer.

18) EEO / demographic optional questions
- Source: employer form.
- Value: left blank unless you instruct otherwise; I will show them on the card and let you choose.

19) Additional message / recruiter note
- Source: short optional message I draft from the posting (<=120 words).
- Value: appears on the card for you to edit.
20) Consent / electronic signature
- Source: your explicit approval on the card; I will not sign or type your legal name without that.
- Value: when you approve the card you will confirm the signature line; nothing is sent until you do.

21) Tracking metadata (internal)
- Value: date prepared, which persona and attachments will be included, any missing required fields, and the next action (queue for submission when you run the extension or prepare an email draft if you asked me to).
- I will show this metadata on the card so you see what's missing and what will happen after you approve.
What I will not do automatically
- I will not submit the application without you approving the card.
- I will not invent facts: any field not already confirmed by you will be shown as a prompt to fill or confirm.
- I will not attach files I don't have or send emails without you enabling your email connection and approving the message.
How the card will show missing or sensitive fields
- Any missing required field (email, resume file, right-to-work) will be flagged with a short prompt and cannot be submitted until you fill it.
- Any screening question that could disqualify you (visa status, criminal history) will be shown with the exact question and my suggested truthful answer; you must approve it.
Final action after you approve the card
- The card gives two final actions: "Queue for your browser extension to submit" (what happens if you run the Trainee extension on your computer) or "Prepare email draft" (if you have enabled email sending and want me to prepare the message). Nothing is sent until you take that final action.
